stages.description: Basic overlap chunking, single retrieval pass, TF-IDF vectorstore
stages.failure_pattern: Missed at least one required clause on 9 of 14 multi_clause_synthesis questions — the general rule and the grade override don't share enough vocabulary to co-rank in one top-k pull.

stages.description: Iterative retrieval (app/advanced/multihop/), reformulating the query using evidence from the previous hop

metrics.note_on_llm_calls: average hops before the sufficiency check is satisfied, across the test set

stages.failure_pattern: Recall improved sharply on multi_clause_synthesis (9/14 missed -> 2/14 missed). Context precision dropped slightly since later hops pull in some tangential context. Cross-reference questions still weak without explicit reference-following.

stages.description: Multi-hop retrieval running against a RAPTOR tree (app/advanced/raptor/) instead of the flat index, plus explicit cross-reference resolution

metrics.note_on_llm_calls: includes cluster-summary generation cost amortized per query, plus hop reasoning calls

stages.failure_pattern: Cross-reference questions improved (2/5 missed -> 0/5 missed) once explicit reference-following was added. Thematic-summary questions (only answerable from a summary node, not any single leaf) went from unanswerable under stages 1-2 to fully correct here — this is RAPTOR's specific contribution, not multi-hop's.

stages.description: Same retrieval quality as stage 3, but repeated queries against the same policy-scenario tuple are served from cache (app/advanced/caching/) instead of re-running retrieval + reasoning

metrics.note: Caching does not change retrieval QUALITY metrics (recall/precision/faithfulness/relevancy are identical to stage 3) — it only changes cost and latency, and only on repeated scenarios. This is why it's reported as a separate axis rather than folded into the RAGAS table above it.

stages.failure_pattern: None specific to caching itself — the risk here is operational (stale cache after a policy change), not a retrieval-quality regression. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for the invalidation design.

summary_takeaways: Recall is the metric that separates the architectures, not top-line accuracy — flat RAG's failure mode is structural (scattered clauses don't co-rank), not a matter of tuning top_k.

RAPTOR's marginal contribution over multi-hop alone is concentrated in thematic-summary and cross-reference questions specifically, not across the whole test set uniformly. This is the empirical basis for scoping RAPTOR to Hop 1 rather than applying it everywhere.

Cost scales with sophistication (0 -> 2.4 -> 3.1 LLM calls/query) unless caching amortizes it, which is why stage 4 exists as a distinct row rather than assuming stage 3's cost is unavoidable in production.
